newsitem.title: UK: Manchester bomb hits insurers for 200 mln stg - ABI.
newsitem.headline: Manchester bomb hits insurers for 200 mln stg - ABI.

text.p: The IRA bomb explosion in Manchester in June has so far cost UK-based insurers nearly 200 million stg, the Association of British Insurers said.

Initial verbal estimates from insurers in the immediate aftermath of the bombing were around 100 million stg. The ABI said gross incurred claims during the second quarter for the Manchester bomb totalled 192 million stg, while London's Docklands bomb in February led to claims of 39 million stg.
For the Manchester bomb, industrial and commercial fire claims accounted for 138 million stg and business interruption claims 54 million stg.
However, the risk incurred by most of these insurers is limited to about 100,000 stg per head of cover because of protection taken out with bomb reinsurer Pool Re.
Nobody was immediately available for comment at Pool Re.
Total insurance payouts across all main sectors jumped during the second quarter from levels last year, said the ABI.
Weather damage claims more than doubled to 113 million stg from 55 million stg, while domestic subsidence payouts leapt by over 130 percent to 70 million stg from 30 million stg.

"After a period of stable or falling claims on non-life policies, the jump in insurance payouts in the second quarter of this year comes as a big disappointment," said Mark Boleat, the director general of the ABI.
"While these figures clearly show the value of insurance, they do add pressure on the industry for rate increases after a long period of largely stable or falling premium levels."
The cost of theft, fire, subsidence and weather claims all increased. Theft rose 13 percent and fire increased 30 percent.
